Tooltip_morphine:
Instantly restores health, kills all pain, clears the mind. Does not heal wounds.
Highly addictive.
Tooltip_naloxone:
Opioid antagonist. Eases addiction.
Leaves you hungry and parched.
Tooltip_fentanyl:
Restores health and erases every wound and treatment (bullets, glass and the virus stay). Kills all pain, clears the mind.
Extremely addictive.
Tooltip_oxycontin:
Mild opioid. Restores some health, calms the mind, eases withdrawal.
Somewhat addictive.
Tooltip_sufentanil:
Patch on the right upper arm: for days it eases pain and withdrawal and keeps you calm, while addiction quietly deepens.
Peel off to stop.
Tooltip_methamphetamine: Instantly wide awake. Feeds amphetamine addiction hard -- the crash will come.
Tooltip_tranexamicacid:
Clots most of the bleeding; the clot settles as a heavier wound.
Dizzy weakness, nausea, lingering headache.
Tooltip_sulfadimidine:
Burns down most of a wound infection per dose; heavy infections take several courses and heal into heavier wounds. No effect on the zombie virus.
Head pain, a lingering fever, kidney strain, nausea.
Tooltip_dexmedetomidine:
Small-animal veterinary sedative. Calm -- or agitation; a coin flip.
Heavy drowsiness, severe head pain.
Tooltip_dextromethorphan:
Cough syrup. Silences sneezing and coughing, helps the cold burn off faster; the rest is up to rest.
Drowsy and parched. Chug it and you pass out.
Tooltip_GrassBandage: Rough grass bandage. Heals far worse than a real one -- and will almost surely infect the wound.
Tooltip_BookSplint: A proper splint lashed from two books and cloth.
Tooltip_TemporarySplint:
Improvised fixation: while worn, the fracture vanishes but the limb's wounds hurt more. A fresh wound on the part breaks it; removal brings the fracture back, worse the longer it was worn.
A full year of wear heals the bone outright.
